name: The last tram on the poem's route
subject: literature
question: meaning
brief: Ms Basu has set a poem called The Last Tram from the Class XI anthology, written by an invented Kolkata poet. It follows an empty tram through the night and ends on the conductor's bell fading as the depot gate closes. What does the poem mean? You write the group's paragraph, and the bell rings in five units.

claims.name: The poem is a farewell to a way of city life that is passing
The poem is about the tram's stubborn survival against the new traffic
The poem is a complaint against the tram company's fare rises

evidence.name: The third stanza counts the empty seats one by one
The last line ends on the conductor's bell fading away
The tram throws sparks from the wire and keeps moving
The poem never mentions a fare, a ticket or a company
The anthology dates the poem to 1974

limitations.name: A farewell reading leans on a reader's own memory of trams, which younger readers may not share
A defiance reading has to explain away the sorrowful last stanza
This is one poem; the poet's other work may treat the tram differently

note: Interpretation has no single hidden right answer (SCHOOL_AND_PROGRESSION.md): two readings are defensible and each has its own evidence and limit. The poet and poem are invented for the alternate world; the tram line is a Kolkata institution.
